_doc: Meshes and lights for Kod-placed objects (data/zone_layout.json objects): `classes` by Kod class ("<Class>/<classtype>" first for an object made with a classtype: "FoodDispenser/Apple" is the apple tree), `types` for OrnamentalObjects by their OO type number (docs/adr/0003 pass 3, docs/adr/0007). tools/ue/build_world.py spawns `mesh` (build/environment/kit/<mesh>.glb: the AI-generated meshes from tools/aigen/aigen.py, data/aigen/props/*.json; skipped until generated) at the object's position, turned (build_world.py prop_yaw): a stable random turn with `random_yaw` (plants and rocks the original drew as camera-facing sprites; it wins over their Kod angle, which the original writes as 0), else the object's Kod angle, else the entry's `facing` ("south" (the model's front, the default), "east", "north", "west" or degrees, UE yaw clockwise from above; signs: east), plus `yaw_offset` degrees, plus a warm point light `offset_m` above it. Light intensity in candela; at ~8 lux of daylight these read as glows and become the main light in deep shade and at night. `light_scale`: one factor on every light the world build adds (props, wall torches, room lights), reach unchanged (2026-10-06: 0.5, the environment carries the scene and fires add warmth). `ambient_scale`: the AI props' ambient floor indoors is the original sector light of the floor under each prop times this (M_PropTextured; 2026-10-07: was a fixed 1, which gave props 4-5x the fill of the Inn's walls). `albedo` (a class): a factor on an AI prop's base colour, for a Tripo texture lighter than the original sprite (2026-10-07: the Inn's Table 0.55 and the Stool 0.56, each from its sprite's mean linear colour against its texture's; the BarStool 0.5, matched to the Table as rendered side by side in the Inn: the sprite method's 0.78 left it 60% brighter). `candela_scale`: a factor on a Kod light's candela (2026-10-06: the braziers and lamps dimmed twice by 25%, to 0.56 of the original, at the user's request: too bright at night). `kod_intensity` / `kod_color` (a light): the Kod class's light (0-255, 15-bit colour), overridden by the object's own iIntensity / iColor; build_world.py turns them into candela (0.24 per unit), reach (4 m + 0.15 per unit) and colour (DynamicLight: the invisible lights the original places in rooms; Candle). `shadows`: false for unshadowed pools of light, as the original's. `night_only` (a light, or a material slot): off from 11 to 17 like the original lamps (kod lamp.kod), switched by the environment director in game (docs/adr/0005). `mesh_custom`: an optional custom model shown instead of `mesh` (a kit GLB name or UE asset path); `mesh` (the HD model) stays the fallback while the custom one doesn't exist. A manifest's `custom` model (tools/aigen) is picked up the same way as `<mesh>_Custom` without an entry here (docs/adr/0007 "Custom models"). `mesh_options` / `mesh_use`: alternative meshes per option ({option: [meshes]}, a stable random variant per object), `mesh_use` picks one option, or "compare" cycles them over the zone's objects of that kind so they stand side by side; `fit_height_m` scales a mesh given as a UE asset path to that height (the trees: AI, procedural Blender kit tools/blender/build_tree_kit.py, Procedural Vegetation Editor exports under /Game/; docs/adr/0007 "Trees"). `blocks` (a class or type): the prop stops players and monsters, with simple collision UE fits around the mesh: true (a 26-sided hull), "box", "capsule" or "sphere" (build_world.py prop_collision); or {"radius_m", "height_m"}: a hidden cylinder at its foot instead, for a tree's trunk or a sign's post (spawn_blocker). 2026-10-07: lamps, braziers, tables, chests, sign posts and tree trunks; every other prop is walked through, as every object in the original. `hanging` (a class or type): hangs from the ceiling above it, its mesh's top at the ceiling, as the original pins OF_HANGING objects (Kod: the Chandelier; OrnamentalObjects with pbHanging, none in the demo); zone_layout.json objects carry the ceiling as `ceiling_y` (build_world.py hanging_y). `lights_at_m` (a hanging class): the height above its mesh's origin where its light sits (the chandelier's candles, 1.1); a DynamicLight on the same spot moves up there (build_world.py lights_to_hanging). `placed`: settings for one placed object by its actor label (Prop_<rid>_<class or OO type>_<index>, as the editor's outliner shows it), over its entry's: e.g. {"Prop_300_Sign_0": {"facing": "north"}} (facing here wins over the Kod angle), or `yaw_offset`, `blocks`: false. `glow` (a class): the lit glass of a lamp on its AI mesh (M_PropTextured PROP_GLOW_HLSL): pale, unsaturated texels inside the lantern, `z_m` [lo, hi] and `radius_m` from the mesh's base centre, in `color` (linear, emissive), off by day with `night_only`; `lum` [lum lo, lum hi, sat, feather] tunes what counts as glass. `highlight` (a light): the original's LIGHT_FLAG_HIGHLIGHT (signs: sign.kod sends white at 255): reach a tenth of a normal light's (d3dlighting.c), a small lit disk at the foot: build_world.py draws it as a spot light `offset_m` above, pointing down, its cone covering that disk on lighting channel 1, which only the room's floors and walls take (not the sign itself). `materials`: the kit's material slots (linear colours; emissive in nits-ish scene units); zone art uses them as 'prop_<name>' slots too (window boxes).

placed._doc: Per placed object, by actor label: any entry setting (facing, yaw_offset, blocks, mesh_custom, ...). Empty until a sign or prop needs its own.

smoke._doc: Chimney smoke (docs/adr/0005 phase 5): tools/environment/chimneys.py finds every chimney the blockout draws with these wall textures, and build_world.py stands a plume (SM_Puffs with M_Smoke, materials.json "smoke") on each top. How much smoke: moods.json "atmosphere" "smoke". A class's "moths": moths circle its light at night, offset_m above the object (SM_Puffs with M_Moth).

fires._doc: Flame presets (docs/adr/0005 phase 3). Each is a flipbook of the original's own flame frames: "texture" (a wall texture's animation frames) or "bgf" + "frames" (an object's, from python tools/bgf2png/bgf2png.py <name>), cropped to "crop" [x0, y0, x1, y1] (original pixels; "keep": "flame" keeps only flame-coloured pixels, "all" every opaque one), upscaled by make_placeholders.py into T_Fire_<name> and drawn by AMRFireActor as a camera-facing sprite at the original's size, cycling at "fps" (each fire from its own phase) with emissive "brightness". "walls": wall textures with this flame painted on (the wall torches): "at" the flame centre in the texture's pixels, "out" the texture direction pointing away from the wall it's mounted on, "erase" the rect whose flame-coloured pixels are made transparent; tools/environment/fires.py finds every flame where the blockout uses them, and "light" lights each (the original torches had none of their own: their sectors were lit). "mesh" (a wall preset): a 3D torch (tools/aigen walltorch) replaces the painted one once its kit mesh exists: make_placeholders.py blanks the torch textures, and build_world.py stands the mesh on each torch's wall (its bracket toward the mesh's -X), its origin at the texture's row "mesh_bottom_px" (the bottom: aigen keeps the empty rows under the torch as the mesh's lift), with the flame on its head sunk "flame_sink_m" into it. A class's "fire": the preset, and "base_m" the height of the flame's bottom above the object. "flicker" on a light: true always, "sector" only in the original's flickering sectors (SF_FLICKER); flickering lights are spawned as AMRFireActor and driven by UMRFireSubsystem (seeded noise, about the original's +-40 of 255, a shadow budget for the nearest few).
